name: xdoc
description:
Convert PPTX decks into PDF, PNG, JSON, and Markdown outputs, and HTML into Markdown.

Accepts single files, multiple files, glob patterns (?/*/**), and
directories. With --recursive, subdirectories are walked.

Shorthand:
  xdoc <inputs...> [options]  ==  xdoc convert <inputs...> [options]

Structured extraction:
  xdoc extract <inputs...> --parts map,resources,notes,links,fonts

HTML to Markdown:
  xdoc html2md page.html --output page.md

Preflight diagnostics:
  xdoc check <inputs...> --checks fonts,links,compat
  xdoc check <inputs...> --checks a11y --pretty

Authorization diagnostics:
  xdoc auth verify --license ./xdoc-license.json

PPTX editing bridge:
  xdoc pptx new --output out.pptx
  xdoc pptx apply --patch patch.json --input in.pptx --output out.pptx

  xdoc pptx inspect deck.pptx --json

  xdoc pptx select deck.pptx --query query.json --json

  xdoc pptx preview deck.pptx --output-dir shots/ --contact-sheet out.png --json

  xdoc pptx chrome-detect deck.pptx --json

  xdoc pptx chrome-remove deck.pptx --roles header,footer,page-number,rule --output clean.pptx

  xdoc pptx chrome-apply deck.pptx --deckkit mckinsey-blue --output styled.pptx

  xdoc pptx refurbish-skin --source old.pptx --deckkit mckinsey-blue --to pdf --output new.pdf

  xdoc pptx apply-brand deck.pptx --brand brand.json --output out.pptx

  xdoc pptx slide-copy target.pptx --source source.pptx --slides 1,3,5-8 --output out.pptx

  xdoc pptx extract-style deck.pptx --output style.json --json

  xdoc pptx import-template reference.pptx --name imported-template --output-dir skills/pptx-nova/assets --json

  xdoc pptx catalog shapes --json

  xdoc pptx catalog themes --json

  xdoc pptx swap-theme deck.pptx --theme corporate-blue --output out.pptx

  xdoc pptx swap-style deck.pptx --style consulting --output out.pptx

  xdoc pptx recipe --recipe recipe.json --compile --json

  xdoc pptx replay --from-sidecar out.pptx.xdoc.json --output recovered.pptx

  xdoc pptx audit --from-sidecar out.pptx.xdoc.json --json

  xdoc pptx rollback --from-sidecar out.pptx.xdoc.json --output recovered.pptx

PDF diagnostics and text extraction:
  xdoc pdf inspect out.pdf --json
  xdoc pdf extract-text input.pdf --json --pretty
  xdoc pdf render input.pdf --pages 1,3-5 --output pages/

Agent stdio protocols:
  xdoc json-rpc
  xdoc mcp

Machine-readable schema:
  xdoc schema

usageNotes: check emits preflight/v1 JSON reports.
Default --checks is the explicit list fonts,links,compat,assets,policy; --checks all adds a11y on top of it.
compat compares the full OOXML package against --target-office (default 365), reports minimumOfficeVersion, and distinguishes unprotected features from mc:Ignorable or AlternateContent fallback.
policy currently runs fixed MVP publishing rules.
a11y runs render-free accessibility rules; see checks.a11y for the rule catalog, the outcome vocabulary, and the declared non-goals.

a11y.reason: The accessibility rules are newer than the publishing diagnostics; they stay out of the default --checks list until the false-positive rate is proven on real decks. --checks all does include them.

rules.summary: Slide has no non-empty title or centered-title placeholder. A visually prominent text box is not accepted as a substitute.
Picture, chart, OLE object, or SmartArt diagram carries neither an accessibility description nor explicit decorative metadata.
A visual relies on the Office 2019 decorative extension, but the requested target Office release predates it and no description fallback exists.
Explicit text color falls below the WCAG-derived minimum contrast ratio against its statically resolved background.
Text has an explicit color but no statically resolvable background color; contrast must be confirmed against a render.

outcomes.violation: The rule was decided and the deck violates it.
outcomes.inconclusive: The rule could not be decided from static package facts; this is never a pass.

checkStatus.passed: Every rule ran and no in-scope finding was produced.
checkStatus.warning: At least one in-scope violation was produced.
checkStatus.inconclusive: No violation, but at least one rule could not be decided.
checkStatus.failed: The scan itself could not run; this is not evidence that the deck is accessible.

findingFields.patchSelector: Ready-to-paste patch selector; its slide field is the zero-based patch index and its shape field uses the numeric cNvPr id.
findingFields.patchTemplate: Present only for the description rules. It contains a placeholder and is deliberately not named fixPatch: autoApplicable is always false and merging it unchanged would write the placeholder text into the deck.
findingFields.evidence: Only the facts the rule actually produced; an omitted field means the rule does not produce it, not that it was checked and empty.

scoping.deckCoverage: Always deck-wide, so a scoped run cannot be mistaken for a full audit.

a11y.targetOfficeInteraction: decorative metadata only exempts a visual from Office 2019 onward; an older --target-office turns it into an explicit a11y_decorative_not_supported finding instead of a silent pass.
a11y.exitCodePolicy: Findings never change the process exit code. A completed scan exits 0 and the verdict is carried by checks.a11y.status, summary.riskLevel, and the report status; only transport, input, and output failures use non-zero exits.
nonGoals: Reading order and tab order are not evaluated.
Table header semantics, merged-cell structure, and complex table navigation are not evaluated.
This is not a full WCAG audit and does not predict screen-reader behavior.
Contrast is derived from statically resolved colors only; gradients, pictures, and pattern fills behind text stay inconclusive rather than passing.
Description quality is not judged; a non-empty description satisfies the rule.

usageNotes: PPTX actions execute inside the xdoc runtime and share its versioned schema and report contract.

Output surfaces follow one rule set: the primary artifact uses --output; outputKind is the default and outputKinds lists any allowed --to selection. For replace-text, replace-chart-text, and refurbish-skin, --to png treats --output as the transactional PNG directory. Other asset-dir actions write through --output-dir and never take --output; a supplementary structured report next to a primary artifact uses --report. No action takes --output and --output-dir together.
Use `xdoc pptx <action> --help` for a low-cost synopsis generated from that action's schema usage, option projections, and examples; use `xdoc schema` for the complete machine contract.
Use action new to create a minimal deck, apply to patch an existing or new deck, or inspect to summarize an existing deck.
For inspect, pass either `xdoc pptx inspect deck.pptx --json` or `xdoc pptx inspect --input deck.pptx --json`.

Use `xdoc pptx morph-check deck.pptx --from-slide 1 --to-slide 2 --json` before authoring Morph, or omit the pair flags to audit every Morph-carrying adjacent pair. The report covers exact case-sensitive `!!` names only and never claims PowerPoint implicit matching or playback parity.

Use `xdoc pptx vision-check deck.pptx --json` to statically QA an existing deck without rendering: it flags geometry overlaps, off-slide and edge-hugging text, text-overflow estimates, unexpected wraps in single-line text roles, misaligned card rows, and sub-threshold fonts, and each issue may carry an auto-applicable fixPatch.

Use `xdoc pptx preview deck.pptx --output-dir shots/ --contact-sheet --contact-output out.png --dpi 192 --json` to render per-slide PNG previews plus an optional contact sheet and stdout manifest for multimodal review.

Use `xdoc pptx visual-audit --candidate new.pptx --reference approved.pptx --output-dir evidence --json` for the canonical Agent visual gate: it atomically writes one typed evidence manifest plus exact PDF/PNG artifacts, separates transport status from check outcomes and Agent action, and limits same-renderer pixel evidence to regression claims rather than PowerPoint parity.

Use `xdoc pptx contact-diff --source old.pptx --candidate new.pptx --output contact-diff.png --dpi 192 --json` to generate a source/candidate side-by-side contact sheet plus changed/unchanged/missing/added slide status; pass `--map reference-map.json` for split/merge/reordered refurbish mapping, pass `--slides 1,3-5` for scoped source-slide review, and treat `agentGate.passed` as pair-integrity readiness for human visual review.

Use `xdoc pptx i18n-scan --source source.pptx --source-lang multi|zh|en --mode source --output i18n-scan.json --json` to persist the full stable i18nUnits inventory while returning only a compact result on stdout; use candidate mode with --output as the authoritative target-consistency gate. Reserve --json-full for interactive debugging of small reports.

Use `xdoc pptx i18n-plan --source old.pptx --units-file i18n-scan-source.json --data translations.json --output i18n-plan.json --json` as the translation planner: agents receive a compact stdout result and read the persisted full plan only when materializing its execution artifacts. Reviewed slide/layout/master units with reviewDecision:"translate" route through the same guarded textPlan, replaceText, or replaceChartText primitives.

entries.summary: Render 3D charts to PDF and preview PNG with explicit fidelity limits.

limits.description: PDF output reproduces PowerPoint's projection, occlusion and default face shading, but not bevel, material or a custom lightRig. c:shape is parsed at both levels but every shape renders as a box, a line3DChart ribbon is drawn as a surface without PowerPoint's ribbon thickness, and a pie3DChart disc has a square edge where PowerPoint bevels it, which shows most at a shallow rotX.

The PDF renderer projects c:bar3DChart, c:line3DChart, c:area3DChart, c:pie3DChart and c:surface3DChart. rotX, rotY, depthPercent, hPercent, gapDepth and perspective drive the projection, walls and depth axis; a pie reads rotX and rotY differently, as its own pitch and slice rotation, and ignores depthPercent as PowerPoint does. c:surfaceChart renders separately as its top-down contour/band view. rAngAx=true is the oblique projection and rAngAx=false a rotated perspective camera, both measured against Microsoft PowerPoint renders; c:perspective maps to a field of view of half its value in degrees, and a pie ignores it.

A surface is coloured by value band and shaded by facet against a measured light rig. Both halves are measured against PowerPoint: the band palette modulates the theme accents by a ladder that the band count selects, matched to within two 8-bit channel steps against PowerPoint's own legend swatches from two through twenty-four bands, and past twenty-four bands the ladder is clamped to the widest measured rung. Rendered meshes agree with PowerPoint to within seven channel steps across that range; the residual tracks the plot rectangle each renderer fits its cube into rather than the light rig. A value axis carrying four bands or fewer uses the accents unmodulated, and there the brightest facet the light rig can produce passes full scale, so a channel already near full — the red of a yellow accent, for instance — clips at full scale instead of carrying the last few percent of its highlight; 8-bit sRGB cannot express that difference and PowerPoint has the same ceiling. Sparse c:bandFmts fill and outline overrides are used exactly as authored, with no ladder applied, but gradient fills degrade to their first stop in native PDF.

Two measured differences remain outside the mesh itself. A c:surface3DChart legend lists the series rather than the value bands PowerPoint lists there, so a 3D surface with a legend shows the wrong entries; the c:surfaceChart top view does list bands. And PowerPoint shades a top-view contour cell by its facet the same way it shades a 3D one, which this renderer does not: flat cells come out right and steep ones render brighter than PowerPoint's.

evidence.claim: Rendering support is tracked separately from native OOXML authoring and never inferred from operation availability.
c:view3D, the three CT_Surface walls, c:gapDepth, both c:shape levels and c:serAx round-trip through both parser engines with matching values.

Both projections are measured against Microsoft PowerPoint renders of a generated calibration corpus: rAngAx=true keeps the category axis horizontal and the value axis vertical while skewing only the depth axis, and rAngAx=false is a rotated camera whose eye distance follows the plot height and c:perspective.

line3DChart and area3DChart render as depth-swept surfaces and solids: a line series is a bare ribbon, an area series the same sweep closed with a cross-section and end caps, and grouping decides whether series occupy their own depth plane.

pie3DChart renders as an extruded disc: rotX sets the ellipse aspect and rim depth, rotY turns the slices, hPercent scales the rim, depthPercent has no effect, and the rim carries the measured cylindrical shading gradient.

surface3DChart renders as a banded height field over the category and series grid: the value axis ticks cut it into bands whose colours follow the accent ladder measured off PowerPoint's legend swatches, each mesh cell is one polygon per band shaded by its own normal, and c:wireframe strokes the same band outlines instead of filling them. The cube's auto height follows a band law measured across twenty-one grids rather than stretching to the plot rectangle.
surfaceChart renders as a top-down category-by-series grid whose values select complete major-tick bands; sparse c:bandFmts, wireframe, axis orientation and missing cells are preserved.

c:majorTickMark and c:minorTickMark are drawn on the category, value and series axes, at the lengths measured off PowerPoint as a fraction of the axis label font. They keep the screen orientation PowerPoint gives them on a projected axis: horizontal on a value axis and vertical on a category axis, even under a perspective camera where the axis itself leans. The same marks are drawn for the 2D chart families.

recommendation.note: Use visual-audit and an independent Office reference before accepting 3D rendering fidelity.

A surface is coloured by value band and shaded by facet against a measured light rig, from the same modules the PDF renderer uses. The band palette modulates the theme accents by a ladder that the band count selects, matched to within two 8-bit channel steps against PowerPoint's own legend swatches from two through twenty-four bands, and past twenty-four bands the ladder is clamped to the widest measured rung. A value axis carrying four bands or fewer uses the accents unmodulated, and there the brightest facet the light rig can produce passes full scale, so a channel already near full — the red of a yellow accent, for instance — clips at full scale instead of carrying the last few percent of its highlight; 8-bit sRGB cannot express that difference and PowerPoint has the same ceiling. Sparse c:bandFmts fill and outline overrides are used exactly as authored, with no ladder applied; the 2D contour keeps SVG gradients, while the shaded 3D surface degrades them to the first stop.

Two measured differences remain outside the mesh itself. A c:surface3DChart legend lists the series rather than the value bands PowerPoint lists there, so a 3D surface with a legend shows the wrong entries; the c:surfaceChart top view does list bands. And PowerPoint shades a top-view contour cell by its facet the same way it shades a 3D one, which this renderer does not: flat cells come out right and steep ones render brighter than PowerPoint's.

i18n-scan.usage: Source inventory: xdoc pptx i18n-scan --source deck.pptx --source-lang multi|zh|en --mode source --output i18n-scan.json --json [--slides 1,3-5]. Candidate gate: xdoc pptx i18n-scan --source candidate.pptx --mode candidate --units-file i18n-scan-source.json --data translations.json --output i18n-candidate.json --json
inputs: candidate PPTX plus source i18nUnits and pptx-i18n-translations/v1 (candidate mode)
outputs: pptx-i18n-scan-result/v1 or pptx-i18n-candidate-result/v1 compact stdout result
i18n-scan.strategy: Source mode opens the PPTX as an OPC package, discovers structurally visible text independently from language confidence, classifies confident source text for translation and ambiguous Latin text for review, includes semantic defaults such as generated classic Chart and ChartEx titles, and emits i18nUnits as the stable agent-facing translation inventory. Candidate mode is the authoritative target-consistency gate: it consumes the source units and translations, locates each translated unit inside the candidate with the source unit selector, and proves currentText equals targetText. hits[] are diagnostic evidence in source mode; agents should not build selectors from hits[].location.

detectors.zh: CJK unified ideograph ranges; no model-based language guessing
detectors.en: Conservative Latin natural-language detection for visible text; standalone URLs, paths, versions, OOXML/code tokens, and known product/tool terms are preserved, while structurally visible ambiguous Latin text is inventoried with action=review instead of disappearing.
detectors.multi: Combined zh + en detector for mixed Chinese/English source decks, especially when translating into a non-English target language.

classes.visibleBody: Slide, notes, table, layout/master, or diagram body text; translate; candidate blocker.
classes.visibleTextAttr: User-visible attributes such as tooltip, descr, and title; translate under controlled replacement; candidate blocker.
classes.chartVisibleCache: Chart title, series, category, and label visible text, including generated classic Chart and ChartEx default titles; translate through guarded chart replacements; candidate blocker.
classes.embeddedWorkbook: Embedded workbook text found inside ppt/embeddings/*.xlsx parts (composite part path workbook.xlsx!xl/...); review required, not a default candidate blocker. Every hit carries an advisory workbookReview with risk, recommendedAction, reason, constraints, and a manual replacementTemplate when the action is not preserve.
classes.relationshipPath: Relationship Target or external path; preserve by default.
classes.shapeInternalName: cNvPr@name authoring identifier; preserve by default.
classes.chartMetadata: Chart metadata such as formatCode; preserve by default.

replacementHints.usage: Use i18nUnits as the stable inventory and let i18n-plan emit replaceText replacements. If manually building replace-text input, copy selectors.replaceText from the unit and add targetText.
replacementHints.indexing: selectors.replaceText.index is the 0-based index expected by replace-text for the given part/tag/attrName stream. hits[].location is a scan diagnostic location and must not be used as replace-text index.
replacementHints.hash: selectors.replaceText.sourceHash includes the sha256: prefix accepted by replace-text.

recommendedAction.translate: Shared string or inline worksheet cell text; translation candidate. Keep item count/order stable and keep chart-backed values in sync with the chart visible cache.
recommendedAction.translate-with-constraints: Table/list-object names; translatable only while the listed identifier constraints hold (uniqueness, no spaces in displayName).
recommendedAction.needs-confirmation: Cell style names, cached <v> values, and unclassified text; decide explicitly per target-locale policy before editing.
recommendedAction.preserve: Sheet/defined names and workbook theme names; chart cache formulas and authoring metadata reference them, so keep the source value.

embeddedWorkbookReview.replacementTemplate: A self-contained manual replacement plan (kind embedded-workbook-text-node|embedded-workbook-text-attr, workbookPart, internalPart, tag/attrName, 0-based same-tag occurrence index, sourceText, sourceHash). No automated xdoc apply path consumes it: replace-text and i18n-plan reject workbook-internal targets. preserve-recommended hits carry replacementTemplate: null.
embeddedWorkbookReview.gate: The recommendation is advisory and never changes gate semantics: every embeddedWorkbook hit stays action=review / recommendedMethod=manual-review. After any manual workbook edit, validate the embedded .xlsx ZIP/XML, keep the chart visible cache in sync, rerun i18n-scan --mode candidate, and check the i18n-style-diff embedded-workbook warnings.

i18nUnits.usage: Primary planner input for xdoc pptx i18n-plan. Translate action=translate units; preserve action=preserve; classify action=review lazily, then authorize reviewed executable units with reviewDecision:"translate" plus sourceHash.

scope.candidate: Candidate mode takes source language and scope from --units-file and rejects --source-lang and --slides so the command line and the contract files cannot disagree.

It does not run the heuristic language classifier, so valid target-language Latin text is never a blocker.

i18n-anchor-draft.strategy: Reuse i18n-plan review/repair material and the current text-plan mapper. The command never rescans XML independently, translates text, mutates a PPTX, or emits executable patch operations.

highConfidence.targetUniqueness: Every candidate anchor occurs exactly once in targetText.
highConfidence.sourceOrder: Multiple candidate anchors occur in the same order as their styled source runs.
highConfidence.usefulToken: Context-inferred candidates are non-empty, not punctuation-only, not repeated significant words, and not short ordinary words. A uniquely preserved exact styled source token is structurally bound and remains eligible regardless of length, including Git and Vue.
highConfidence.contextIsolation: A changed target token is eligible only when unique unchanged neighboring run text isolates exactly one unresolved styled run. Changed CJK wording is never auto-aligned.
highConfidence.plannerValidation: The ordered anchors must be accepted by the existing planner's adjacent plain-run assignment before entering translationsDraft.

blockerCategories.plannerPassthrough: Any i18n-plan conflict category or non-mixed-style review category may also appear verbatim in blocked[].category. Agents must treat unfamiliar categories as fail-closed blockers and follow nextAction.

stdout.format: complete JSON when --json is set; human summary otherwise

filesystem.usage: PPTX and contract inputs are read-only; optional --output persists the report and --overwrite is required to replace it

exitCodePolicy.0: Draft evaluation completed. status may be pass, partial, blocked, or no-op; inspect blocked[] and merge only translationsDraft entries.
exitCodePolicy.2: CLI argument parsing or validation failed.
exitCodePolicy.3: Source/units/translations input is invalid, --unit-id is unknown, or an input contract cannot be parsed. No draft report is trusted.
exitCodePolicy.9: The optional report output could not be created or replaced; the input PPTX and contract files remain untouched.

agentPolicy.entryPoint: Use reviewRequired[].draftCommand/suggestedCommand for a mixed-style-no-anchor unit, or omit --unit-id to triage all scoped units.
agentPolicy.mergePolicy: Merge translationsDraft.translations[] into the existing translations[] array by unitId. Never replace the full translation document with this partial projection and never merge blocked candidates.
agentPolicy.gate: summary.draftCount and translationsDraft.translations.length identify merge material; agentGate.applyAuthorized is always false and plannerRerunRequired is true exactly when draftCount is non-zero.
agentPolicy.applyAuthorization: After merging anchors, rerun i18n-plan using rerunArgs[] or rerunCommand. Only the new plan's applyGate.passed=true authorizes patch/replacement execution.
agentPolicy.fallback: For blocked units, fill the planner's targetSegments repair or obtain manual review. Do not reinterpret candidateAnchors conversationally as high confidence.

i18n-plan.usage: xdoc pptx i18n-plan --source old.pptx --units-file i18n-scan-source.json --data translations.json --output i18n-plan.json --json [--slides 1,3-5]
inputs: pptx-i18n-units/v1 JSON or full i18n-scan report
i18n-plan.strategy: Validate unitId/sourceText/sourceHash guarded translations against the current source inventory, then route each unit to the safest available execution primitive without requiring agents to construct low-level selectors.

translationUnit.guard: sourceHash and sourceText, when present, must match the i18nUnits source unit before any execution plan is emitted. targetSegmentsContractId, when present, must match the current run structure.
translationUnit.anchorsContract: When anchors[] is present, it must contain exactly one non-empty target anchor for every non-empty styled/protected source run, in source-run order. Every anchor must occur exactly once in targetText, counting overlapping matches. When anchors[] is omitted, the planner may only infer a uniquely preserved exact source token for every styled run.
translationUnit.reviewDecision: Set reviewDecision:"translate" together with the unit's sourceHash to apply a reviewed unit's targetText through the standard execution primitives; without it, a review unit carrying targetText stays a review-target conflict. Applied reviewed units are counted in summary.reviewedTranslationCount.

routes.textPlan: DrawingML shape and table paragraphs share the i18n-text-plan run-mapping strategies. Shape targets materialize as guarded set-run patch.ops; table targets materialize as guarded replaceText replacements for existing a:t nodes. The report.textPlan sub-artifact is labelled pptx-i18n-text-plan-input/v1 and is the only valid --data input for i18n-text-plan.
routes.replaceText: User-visible text attributes become replace-text replacements with stable part/tag/attr/index selectors copied from i18nUnits.
routes.replaceChartText: Chart visible text units become replace-chart-text replacements with part/role/nodePath/index selectors copied from i18nUnits. Generated classic Chart and ChartEx title units additionally carry sourceState=generated-default-title, chartDialect, and structureSignature and are materialized only while all guarded state still matches.
routes.reviewedSharedText: A slideLayout or slideMaster unit remains manual-review until translations[].reviewDecision is translate and sourceHash matches. Authorization selects the executable selector already carried by the unit, so shared text uses guarded textPlan/replaceText/replaceChartText instead of remaining permanently review-only.

gates.applyGate: Passed only when the plan has no conflicts, no missing translations, and no apply-blocking review items. Apply generated replacement files and patch.ops only when true.
gates.deliveryGate: Planner deliveryGate is intentionally conservative; final delivery still requires applying to a candidate and passing candidate i18n-scan, i18n-style-diff, preview/visual checks, and text overflow review.

targetSegmentsRepair.eligibility: Emitted only when a text-plan review can be repaired by a complete targetSegments mapping; selector/source/unsupported-method reviews do not receive it.
targetSegmentsRepair.mergePolicy: Copy translationPatchTemplate into the existing translations[] item matched by unitId, fill every null text, and rerun i18n-plan. Do not append a duplicate translation record.
targetSegmentsRepair.failClosed: Templates use text=null and ready=false. The translations parser rejects an unfilled template; completed segments must match group ids/order, targetText reconstruction, sourceHash, and targetSegmentsContractId.

anchorDraftRepair.eligibility: A mixed-style-no-anchor review emits unit-specific draftCommand and suggestedCommand. Other review categories do not advertise the anchor helper.
anchorDraftRepair.flow: Run the command, merge only translationsDraft.translations[] by unitId, then rerun this planner. A draft report never changes applyGate and never authorizes execution.
anchorDraftRepair.fallback: If anchor drafting remains blocked, fill reviewRequired[].repair.translationPatchTemplate targetSegments instead.

stdout.format: compact JSON when --json is set; complete JSON only with --json-full; human summary otherwise

filesystem.usage: PPTX and contract inputs are read-only; --output persists the complete pptx-i18n-plan/v1 report and --overwrite is required to replace it

exitCodePolicy.0: Plan status is pass and applyGate can pass.
exitCodePolicy.2: CLI argument parsing or validation failed.
exitCodePolicy.3: Invalid source/units/translations input, or a completed plan whose status is not pass: blocked (conflicts), review-required (apply-blocking reviews), or incomplete (missing translations). A completed --json request still emits one compact result and --output, when supplied, contains the complete plan.
exitCodePolicy.9: The complete plan could not be persisted to --output; no execution artifact is trusted from that invocation.

agentPolicy.preferredFlow: i18n-scan source -> fill pptx-i18n-translations/v1 by unitId -> i18n-plan -> apply generated replaceChartText/replaceText/patch artifacts -> final delivery gates.
agentPolicy.fallback: Use i18n-text-plan, replace-text, or replace-chart-text directly only when debugging or manually handling a planner output; do not hand-derive selectors from scan diagnostics.
agentPolicy.repairFlow: When reviewRequired[].repair is present, consume its sourceRunGroups/sourceSequence and merge the filled translationPatchTemplate by unitId before rerunning i18n-plan; never guess sourceRunGroupId values.
agentPolicy.reviewFlow: For action=review units, decide translate/preserve from context, then supply reviewDecision:"translate" plus the unit's sourceHash in translations[] instead of hand-building replace-text inputs; the planner materializes the reviewed target through the same guarded artifacts.
agentPolicy.triage: Start from applyGate.blockingReviewCount, applyGate.conflictCount, and applyGate.blockersByCategory; reviewRequired[] lists apply-blocking items first, so repair top-down instead of filtering the whole array.

i18n-text-plan.strategy: Inspect existing DrawingML text and structural nodes, map ordinary runs without rebuilding paragraphs, and preserve break/tab/field identity through one guarded atomic structured-paragraph operation.

translationUnit.note: Use the report.textPlan sub-artifact emitted by `xdoc pptx i18n-plan`. The top-level unitId-based pptx-i18n-translations/v1 document is not valid input here and is rejected with a targeted error.
translationUnit.indexing: slide is 1-based; paragraph is 0-based; shapeId is the source PPTX cNvPr id.

strategies.uniform: Single source run receives the full target text.
strategies.preserve-run-boundaries: Multiple source runs share one style signature; the first run receives the full target and continuation runs are cleared while their style nodes remain.
strategies.preserve-styled-token-boundaries: Mixed-style runs keep styled token anchors in their original run boundaries and distribute surrounding target text to adjacent plain runs.
strategies.preserve-anchor-boundaries: Uniquely ordered anchors map protected hyperlink groups to target text, then pass the same exact segment reconstruction validator before patch ops are emitted.
strategies.structured-target-segments: Explicit targetSegments map translated text to every sourceRunGroupId when hyperlink boundaries or mixed styles cannot be inferred safely.
strategies.preserve-structural-boundaries: Break and tab delimiters partition target text into editable segments; fields stay immutable and are represented as {{field:N}} placeholders. One atomic patch validates the typed node sequence before replacing ordinary runs.
strategies.review-required: The planner could not prove a safe run-level mapping; do not auto-apply the unit.

inputs: one optional source-slide selector; omitting all selectors copies the first source slide

selection.slides: --slides N|N-M[,N|N-M...] selects one or more 1-based source slides in caller order; omitting every selector copies the first source slide
selection.all: --all selects every source slide in source order

template.register-source: Faithfully registers the selected source layout/master/theme closure, reusing a normalized registered closure when equivalent and copying only selected layouts rather than every sibling layout.
template.rebind-target: Explicitly points copied slides at an existing registered target layout and reports inherited-style fidelity risk when the closures differ.

slideSize.require-match: Blocks preflight when source and target p:sldSz differ; no renderer or geometry layer performs implicit scaling.

slide-copy.notes: Opens the target and source once, computes a read-only dependency and registration plan without serializing or mutating either deck, and applies that exact fingerprint-bound plan on an in-memory candidate only when no blocker exists. Registration allocates target-side master/layout ids and relationship ids, deterministically merges content types and part names, and rebuilds only the selected layout registry.

report.status: always success; outcome is passed for an approved plan and blocked when dependencies are unsafe
report.copied: per-slide 0-based source/target indexes, planned slide part mappings, and dependency mappings
report.dependencyMappings: flattened aggregate dependency mappings with owning sourceSlide and targetSlide
report.changedParts: deduplicated target part names the approved plan will mutate
report.transaction: entire-copy-batch rollback boundary plus affected source slides and target slide-count range
report.preflight: read-only source/target file SHA-256 values plus normalized OPC package fingerprints, explicit strategies, template source-to-target mappings/fingerprints/outcomes/registration ids, target slide counts, SHA-256 identified parts, normalized relationship edges, add/reuse/rename/rebind/inspect decisions, blockers, preserve-only/fidelity risks, and action counts

mvpLimits: Does not write apply sidecars because it is not a replayable patch op
The only slide-size strategy is require-match; mismatched decks fail closed until an explicit audited geometry policy is implemented

fill.description: Exactly one fill kind: solid, gradient, pattern, or none.

shapeFill.description: Exactly one fill kind for a shape: solid, gradient, pattern, none, or picture. Picture is shape-only; slide background, table cell, chart and master fills use the fill definition.

gradientStop.description: pos/position is a 0..1 fraction along the gradient axis (serialized as a:gs pos 0..100000).

line.description: Sparse outline override; width follows the length rules ('1pt'). noLine removes the outline; clearDash resets an inherited dash.

shapeAccessibilityPatch.description: Local accessibility metadata stored on the selected shape's cNvPr. Omit a field to preserve it and use null to clear it. title and description accept non-blank strings; description maps to OOXML descr. decorative accepts an explicit boolean and maps to the Office 2019 adec:decorative extension without changing title or description.

title.description: Optional short accessibility title. Omit to preserve, null to clear, or provide a non-blank string to set.

description.description: Optional accessibility description, serialized as cNvPr@descr. Omit to preserve, null to clear, or provide a non-blank string to set.

decorative.description: Optional Office 2019 decorative flag. Omit to preserve, null to remove the recognised extension, or provide true/false to retain that explicit Boolean value.

shadowEffect.description: angle is degrees clockwise from the positive x-axis (0..<360); distance and blur follow the length rules; alpha is 0..1 opacity.

font.description: Sparse font override. Omitted name/eastAsian/complexScript/spacing keys preserve the local value; null clears it so inheritance resumes. name maps a:latin, eastAsian maps a:ea, complexScript maps a:cs, and spacing maps rPr/defRPr@spc in hundredths of a point. size follows the general length rules. spacing accepts only an explicit pt string from -4000pt through 4000pt or a numeric raw-EMU value in the equivalent range; percentages and other unit strings are rejected.

chartDateAxis.description: Explicit native c:dateAx creation for add-chart. When type=date is present, data.categories must contain strict Gregorian ISO YYYY-MM-DD dates in the 1900-01-01..9999-12-31 range; the runtime writes Excel 1900-system serials to the chart cache and embedded workbook. Omission never infers date semantics. Only classic category-axis chart kinds accept this object; chartEx/dataEx, pie/doughnut, scatter/bubble, stock, and combo charts reject it.

chartExData.description: Semantic data for Office chartEx modern charts. Use with add-chart/set-chart-data as dataEx for waterfall, funnel, histogram, treemap, sunburst, or boxWhisker.

hierarchyChartExData.description: Hierarchy data for treemap and sunburst. For set-chart-data.dataEx, include kind/chartKind/type when the target chart kind is ambiguous.

comboChartData.description: Combo chart data. Each series declares kind=column|line|area and may set secondaryAxis=true to use a right-side secondary value axis.

stockChartData.description: Stock chart data for HLC and OHLC stock charts; high, low, close are required and open is optional. All value arrays must match categories length.

tableCellStyle.description: Cell style payload. row/col are zero-based; styling a spanned merged cell is rejected, while the merge-origin cell may be styled.

tableCellBorders.description: Per-edge table border model. top/right/bottom/left apply to cell edges or a range outline; insideH/insideV apply only through set-table borders ranges; cross applies both diagonal cell lines.

oneOf.description: Table shape name shorthand for AI-facing table cell payloads.

verticalAnchor.description: Vertical anchoring of text inside its frame; serialized as bodyPr anchor t/ctr/b.

oneOf.description: Legacy shorthand. 'blank' selects the blank layout; known OOXML layout type strings select by type; other strings select by layout name.

layoutContractSelector.description: Built-in layout content contract selector from commands.pptx.catalogs.layouts.

layoutContractContent.description: Content payload for one of the six built-in Draft 2020-12 layout contracts.

path.description: Relative path resolved inside xdoc pptx apply --asset-root; defaults to the patch file directory when --asset-root is omitted.

oleProgId.description: OLE ProgID string. Common Excel, Word, PDF, Equation, and Package values are shown as examples; custom ProgID strings are accepted.

paragraphAlignment.description: Serialized as a:pPr algn; 'justify-low' and 'thai-distribute' are the East-Asian justification variants.

textFrameAutofitPatch.description: 'none' keeps the frame fixed, 'shape' grows the shape to fit the text, 'text' shrinks text on overflow (fontScale is a percent, text mode only); null clears the autofit setting.

textFramePatch.description: Text-frame layout patch. Omitted fields preserve the current OOXML value; null removes the explicit bodyPr attribute or child so defaults apply again. Margins use signed Length values and are not silently clamped to the shape bounds.

oneOf.description: Line multiple; PowerPoint single line = 1.0 and serializes as spcPct val=100000
Fixed line spacing length; serialized as spcPts

paragraphBullet.description: Discriminated by type; 'none' removes the bullet and 'character' requires char.

slideSize.description: 'standard' is 4:3 and 'wide' is 16:9; explicit w/h follow the length rules.

chartVariant.description: Variant matrix: bar/column/bar3D=clustered|stacked|percent-stacked; column3D=standard|clustered|stacked|percent-stacked; area/area3D=standard|stacked|percent-stacked; line=standard|markers|stacked|percent-stacked; line3D=standard; scatter=markers|lines|lines-no-markers|smooth|smooth-no-markers; pie/pie3D/doughnut=standard|exploded; surface/surface3D=standard|wireframe; stock=standard.

oneOf.description: PowerPoint built-in chart style index serialized as c:style val=1..48.
Clear the explicit c:style element.

chartMarker.description: size is in points (2..72); fill and line take hex colors.

chartLabelScope.description: Data label scope. Omit (or use an empty object) for plot 0; use {plot} for a plot, {series} for a series, or {series, point} for a single point. plot cannot be combined with series or point.

chartDataLabelPosition.description: 'above'/'below' are the line/scatter spellings serialized as OOXML t/b; legal positions depend on the chart kind (bars use inside/outside-end, pie uses best-fit).

chartTickMark.description: Serialized as OOXML c:majorTickMark / c:minorTickMark cross|in|none|out. An axis that omits the element renders as 'cross', the schema default. The PDF, preview and viewer renderers draw the marks in the axis line's colour and width, and draw none when that line is set to no fill.

legendPosition.description: Serialized as c:legendPos (top-right = 'tr'); setting a position implies the legend is shown.

index.description: 0-based plot index within the chart part.

firstSliceAngle.description: Pie/doughnut first slice angle in degrees (c:firstSliceAng).

oneOf.description: Restore the automatic base time unit (removes c:baseTimeUnit).

baseTimeUnit.description: Date-axis category grouping unit (c:baseTimeUnit). Only an existing date axis (c:dateAx) accepts it; category/value axes reject the op.

oneOf.description: Restore the automatic major time unit (removes c:majorTimeUnit).

majorTimeUnit.description: Date-axis major tick interval unit (c:majorTimeUnit); majorUnit gives the count. Only an existing date axis (c:dateAx) accepts it.

oneOf.description: Restore the automatic minor time unit (removes c:minorTimeUnit).

minorTimeUnit.description: Date-axis minor tick interval unit (c:minorTimeUnit); minorUnit gives the count. Only an existing date axis (c:dateAx) accepts it.

chartAxisScalePatch.description: min/max/majorUnit/minorUnit are in axis value units; base/major/minorTimeUnit apply only to an existing date axis, and null restores the automatic setting.

labelOffset.description: Category-axis label distance from the axis in percent (100 = default).

rotation.description: Tick label rotation in degrees, written as a:bodyPr rot (1 deg = 60000).

chartDataLabelsPatch.description: Data-label mutation shared by classic and ChartEx charts. Classic chart point scope supports position and font; point fonts are written to the matching c:dLbl/c:txPr/a:p/a:pPr/a:defRPr without changing sibling point labels. On ChartEx, position maps to cx:dataLabels@pos and showValue/showCategoryName/showSeriesName map to cx:visibility@value/categoryName/seriesName. On ChartEx, font writes the default label font into cx:dataLabels/cx:txPr (a:p/a:pPr/a:defRPr), creating the text body when absent. ChartEx rejects point scope and the unsupported showPercentage/showLegendKey/numberFormat/separator fields instead of silently dropping them.

oneOf.description: Show every label again (removes all cx:dataLabelHidden entries).

hiddenPoints.description: ChartEx only: complete replacement list of zero-based UInt32 data-point indexes (0..4294967295) whose labels are hidden (cx:dataLabelHidden@idx). The list replaces all existing entries; duplicates are deduplicated and output is written in ascending order. [] or null removes every existing hidden entry; when cx:dataLabels is absent, clearing is a preserve-first no-op and does not create an empty container. Classic (c:) charts reject this field.

mode.description: stretch scales one copy of the image to the fill rectangle; tile repeats it.

fillPicture.description: Image fill (a:blipFill) for a shape. assetSource is resolved to bytesBase64 + mimeType by xdoc before apply. mode defaults to stretch and tile requires mode=tile. Recolor effects such as duotone are not part of this payload.

align.description: a:tile@algn anchor for the first tile.

flip.description: a:tile@flip mirror mode for alternating tiles.

pictureFillTile.description: a:tile parameters for a tiled picture fill. scaleX/scaleY are fractions of the natural image size (1 = 100%); omitted fields keep the DrawingML default.

slideTarget.description: targetSlide is a zero-based slide index.

secondaryAxis.description: When true, plot this combo series against a right-side secondary value axis.

oneOf.description: Remove the generated equation/R-squared label formatting container.

rotation.description: Generated label rotation in degrees, written as a:bodyPr rot (1 degree = 60000).

order.description: Polynomial order; only valid with type polynomial.

period.description: Moving-average period; only valid with type moving-average.

chartTrendlineSpec.description: order applies only to polynomial (2..6) and period only to moving-average (>= 2); label requires displayEquation or displayRSquared to be true.

oneOf.description: Remove all trendlines from the series.
Remove all trendlines from the series.
Replace the complete ordered trendline collection; [] removes all entries.
Remove the axis title.

rotation.description: Title text rotation in degrees, written as a:bodyPr rot (1 deg = 60000).

oneOf.description: Remove these gridlines.
Remove value-axis display units.
Custom display-unit divisor written as c:custUnit.

showLabel.description: Show the display-units label next to the axis (c:dispUnitsLbl).

oneOf.description: Remove error bars from the series.

value.description: Error amount for fixed / percentage / std-dev value types.

chartErrorBarsPatch.description: valueType 'custom' requires the plus/minus value arrays; null removes the error bars.

oneOf.description: Remove the data table.

rotX.description: c:rotX rotation around the X axis in degrees; null removes the element.

rotY.description: c:rotY rotation around the Y axis in degrees; null removes the element.

rightAngleAxes.description: c:rAngAx right-angle-axes flag. True keeps the two data axes at right angles and skews only the depth axis, and perspective then has no effect; false is a rotated perspective camera. An omitted element renders as true.

perspective.description: c:perspective viewing angle: the vertical field of view is half this value in degrees, so 0 is orthographic. Only applies while rightAngleAxes is false. Null removes the element.

depthPercent.description: c:depthPercent chart depth as a percentage of the chart base, which PowerPoint measures as one category band rather than the whole plot width; null removes the element.

heightPercent.description: c:hPercent chart height as a percentage of chart width. Omitting the element is not the same as 100: with no c:hPercent the plot cube stretches to fill the plot area, while an explicit value fixes its aspect. Null removes the element.

chartView3DPatch.description: c:view3D scene of a 3D chart. Requires a 3D chart group (bar3DChart, line3DChart, area3DChart, pie3DChart, surface3DChart, surfaceChart) and fails closed otherwise. Both the PDF renderer and the bundled Viewer project bar3DChart, line3DChart, area3DChart, pie3DChart and surface3DChart from the same measured geometry, held together by checked-in vertex vectors; surfaceChart renders separately as the top-down contour/band view of the same data. A pie reads the scene differently: rotX is its pitch, rotY turns its slices, hPercent scales its rim, and depthPercent and perspective do nothing, as in PowerPoint. A surface differs again: with no hPercent its cube is sized from the mesh rather than stretched to the plot area.

chartColorStyleMethod.description: How PowerPoint expands the color cycle across series (cs:colorStyle@meth): cycle repeats the list in order; the linear variants interpolate luminance within one color or across the whole cycle.

chartColorStylePatch.description: Complete replacement for the chart's color style part (cs:colorStyle, the colors*.xml sibling of the chart part). colors is the full series color cycle in order — PowerPoint assigns colors[i % n] to series i whenever a series has no inline fill override, for both classic (c:) and chartEx (cx:) charts. Existing cs:variation children and the style-family id attribute are preserved; method maps onto the meth attribute and keeps its current value when omitted (new parts default to cycle). When the chart has no color style part one is created next to the chart part and wired into [Content_Types].xml plus the chart relationships. A part shared by several charts recolors all of them; apply reports a chart-color-style warning with the reference count.

data.admission: Bounded by maxConnections; saturation leaves later connections in the kernel listen backlog.

control.admission: Dedicated sequential listener outside data-plane maxConnections admission.

statuses.running: The daemon is reachable and accepting work.
statuses.stopping: The daemon accepted shutdown and is draining accepted handlers.
statuses.draining: The same-revision pid is alive but its control listener is unreachable; mutation fallback must fail closed.
statuses.stale: A live pid is recorded by an incompatible or malformed state file and must be retired before replacement.
statuses.stopped: No live daemon owner is recorded.

observability.activeConnections: Accepted data-plane connections whose handlers have not completed.
observability.activeMutations: PPTX apply requests that acquired their session FIFO and entered protected mutation.
observability.mutationStartedCount: Cumulative protected mutations entered since daemon start.
observability.mutationCompletedCount: Cumulative protected mutations released since daemon start.

usageNotes: Use `xdoc daemon start` to run the foreground loopback daemon for Agent multi-step PPTX editing.
Use `xdoc daemon status --json` to distinguish running, stopping, draining, stale, and stopped lifecycle states.
Use `xdoc daemon stop` to ask the reachable daemon to shut down and remove its state file.
The daemon listens only on IPv4 loopback. XDOC_DAEMON_PORT selects the data endpoint port; the state file publishes both port and controlPort.

Each TCP connection carries one request. Data-plane connections are bounded by maxConnections; saturation leaves later connections in the kernel listen backlog instead of creating an unbounded application queue.
Status and shutdown use a dedicated control endpoint outside data-plane admission, so shutdown remains reachable while every data connection is occupied.
Data frames are bounded by maxFrameBytes. Control frames use controlMaxFrameBytes and controlFrameTimeoutMs so a partial control client cannot monopolize lifecycle operations.

Status exposes activeConnections, activeMutations, mutationStartedCount and mutationCompletedCount. In a controlled probe with no unrelated applies, cumulative counter deltas can prove that a previously active mutation remained in flight across snapshots; these aggregates are not per-mutation identifiers.

Inspect and apply are FIFO-serialized per filesystem-identity deck session; symlink, hard-link and host case/separator aliases share one history, while different deck sessions may execute concurrently.
Deck sessions are pruned by idle timeout and max-session limits, but leased sessions are never pruned.
Shutdown closes both listeners, rejects undispatched business requests with ShuttingDown, and drains already accepted handlers without preempting mutations.

environment.XDOC_DAEMON_PORT: Override the IPv4 loopback data-plane port, default 0 for an OS-assigned port; the host is fixed to 127.0.0.1.
environment.XDOC_DAEMON_IDLE_MS: Override deck session idle timeout, default 300000.
environment.XDOC_DAEMON_MAX_CONNECTIONS: Override maximum active data-plane TCP connections, default 64. The dedicated control endpoint is not counted.
environment.XDOC_DAEMON_AUTO_SPAWN: Set to 0 or false to disable pptx --daemon auto-spawn.
environment.XDOC_DAEMON_LOG: Override auto-spawn daemon stdout/stderr log path, default $TMPDIR/xdoc-daemon.log.

json-rpc.description: Serve newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout for AI Agents.

stdout.format: ndjson

framing.idRule: String ids are bounded by maxIdBytes; numeric ids must be safe integers; null is accepted but discouraged by JSON-RPC 2.0.
framing.batch: A non-empty JSON array is one frame; batch items execute serially and responses are returned as one array after progress notifications.
framing.stdout: Protocol frames only; logs and diagnostics use stderr.

ordering.scope: one process and one shared PPTX session runtime
ordering.backpressure: The server reads the next frame only after the current frame is fully handled and flushed.

lifecycle.start: Launch `xdoc json-rpc`; no initialize handshake is required.
lifecycle.shutdown: Send xdoc.shutdown as a request with an id; the process exits after flushing that frame's response.
lifecycle.abruptEnd: Closing stdin ends the process cleanly after the active synchronous request returns.

notifications.responseRule: A frame with no id member never receives a response, including when it is malformed.
notifications.malformedRule: A malformed notification is reported on stderr and produces no protocol frame, because JSON-RPC 2.0 forbids answering one and silence alone would hide the mistake.
notifications.requestOnlyBehavior: A request-only method sent as a notification is ignored without mutation and reported on stderr.

progress.semantics: Best-effort operation-boundary progress; no fractional progress is promised.

cancellation.semantics: Cooperative queued cancellation only. The serial native MVP cannot interrupt an already-dispatched method; cancellation can suppress a later request in the same batch or a subsequently received request with that id.
cancellation.resultRule: Sent as a request it answers with the standard result envelope, whose value carries the accepted flag.

pptx.apply.conditionalRequirement: outputPath is required unless dryRun is true
pptx.apply.assetRule: patch is an object; assetSource paths are materialized relative to assetRoot before dispatch and are bounded by the same CLI asset policy.

resultEnvelope.value: The exact structured report produced by the shared xdoc business handler.
resultEnvelope.artifacts: Explicit file references; binary payloads are never written to protocol stdout.

usageNotes: Keep one process alive to reuse parsed PPTX sessions across requests.
Send xdoc.capabilities to retrieve the same protocol contract without invoking `xdoc schema`.
Treat stdout as a protocol channel; never parse stderr as JSON-RPC.
Use pptx.apply with an id so mutation failures cannot be discarded as notification errors.

mcp.description: Serve the Model Context Protocol over stdin/stdout for MCP clients.

stdout.format: ndjson

protocolVersions.unsupported: No 2024 revision is served. A 2024 initialize is counter-offered 2025-11-25 and never negotiated.
protocolVersions.eraRule: One connection serves one era. A probe may still fall back to initialize, but after a business request in one era the other era's opening is refused.

framing.batch: Rejected; stdio carries one JSON-RPC message per line.
framing.idRule: A request id must be a string within maxIdBytes or a safe integer; MCP does not accept a null id.
framing.stderr: Logs and diagnostics; a client must not read it as failure.
framing.eof: Closing stdin finishes the request in flight, flushes, and exits 0. There is no shutdown method or tool.
